title: Slab-built rectangular serving board
subtitle: A flat clay board with a low raised rim, no kiln required
excerpt: A rectangular slab board with a raised rim on all four sides forms a shallow tray for displaying cheese or bread. This version is built in air-dry clay with a 6 mm base slab and 12 mm rim walls, and requires no kiln. Once sealed it makes a decorative serving surface, not for wet or hot food.
sourceNotes: Technique derived from first principles. Slab-building methods referenced from Encyclopedia Britannica 11th edition (1911) pottery entry. V&A open-access collection for historical ceramic flatware form reference.

glossaryTerms.definition: A flat sheet of clay rolled to an even thickness, used as the building unit in slab construction
The joining method for clay: roughen both surfaces with a needle, apply clay slip, then press together

content.text: A rectangular slab board is a flat clay base with a low wall around the perimeter, forming a shallow open tray about 25 cm x 15 cm. The base is a rolled
slab

and the rim walls are strips attached by score-and-slip. This design works in air-dry clay with no kiln: it sets at room temperature over two to three days. Once sealed, the board works as a display tray for cheese, charcuterie, or bread at a table.

materials.name: Clay slip (same clay body thinned with water)
PVA glue diluted 50/50 with water (for sealing)

content.text: Preparation

Work on a canvas sheet or lightly dusted board. Cut all pieces in one session so the base and walls are at a matching moisture level when joined. Keep unworked clay sealed in a bag. Prepare a small pot of clay slip (a golf-ball of clay dissolved in a tablespoon of water, stirred to a thick cream) before starting.
Rolling and cutting the base
Roll the clay to 6 mm thick using guide sticks placed either side of the clay. A rolling pin run along the guide sticks levels the slab in two or three passes.
Cut a rectangle 25 cm x 15 cm for the base. Use a straight-edged ruler and a fettling knife. Cut in one firm pass rather than sawing, to keep the edge clean.
Lift the base slab onto a flat board lined with paper. Smooth the surface lightly with a damp sponge.
Cutting and attaching the rim walls
Roll a second slab to 6 mm. Cut four rim strips: two at 25 cm x 12 mm (long sides) and two at 15 cm x 12 mm (short sides). These will form the low raised border around the base.
Allow the base and rim strips to stiffen for 20 to 30 minutes on the canvas so they hold their shape during joining. They should be firm but not yet
leather-hard
Use the
score-and-slip

method to attach each rim strip. Score the base perimeter and the bottom edge of each strip with a needle tool, covering both faces with a cross-hatch of shallow scratches. Apply clay slip to both scored faces. Press the strip upright along the edge of the base and hold for 15 to 20 seconds.
Work around the board in order: both long sides first, then both short sides. The short side strips butt up against the ends of the long strips at each corner.

Blend each interior join line with a wooden rib, pressing clay into the corner to fill any gap. Smooth with a barely damp sponge. Check that all four walls stand vertical; press gently to correct any lean.

A slab board is a flat clay base with low walls. It makes a shallow tray about 25 cm x 15 cm. Roll the base as a slab. Cut strips for the walls. Join them with score-and-slip. No kiln is needed. The clay sets at room temperature in two to three days. Seal it well. Use it as a tray for cheese, bread, or charcuterie.
Drying

Place the board on a flat surface. The base is the widest piece in the set and is most prone to warping: dry it on a surface that allows even airflow underneath, such as a board raised slightly on supports, or flip it carefully to its base once the walls have firmed. Cover loosely with a cloth for the first 24 hours to slow drying and reduce warping. After 24 hours, remove the cloth and allow the board to air-dry fully to
bone-dry
: pale, lightweight, and no longer cold to the touch. This typically takes two to four days at room temperature.
Sealing and finishing

Sand any rough edges gently with fine sandpaper before sealing. Apply two coats of 50/50 PVA and water to all surfaces, top, base, and all four exterior rim faces, allowing each coat to dry fully between applications. The seal makes the surface wipe-clean and reduces dust absorption. For a warmer finish, apply a coat of clear acrylic varnish over the dried PVA.
Use and care

This board is a decorative display surface. Air-dry clay is not food-safe without a tested glaze, and it is not waterproof. Use it to display dry cheese portions, wrapped charcuterie, or a bread loaf on a board liner. Do not place hot dishes directly on the clay surface. Wipe with a dry cloth; do not submerge in water or put in a dishwasher.
Variations
Press leaf impressions or a lace border into the base slab before it stiffens. Once the board is sealed and dry, paint the impressed lines with acrylic paint. This adds a more decorative surface.
Make a smaller version at 15 cm x 10 cm as a ring or trinket dish with a 10 mm rim, a useful desk or dressing-table piece.
Cut the rim strips at 20 mm height rather than 12 mm for a deeper tray that can hold small flat items such as coasters or business cards.
Troubleshooter

items.problem: Base warps upward at the corners during drying
items.cause: The base slab is drying faster on the top face than the bottom, pulling the edges up
items.fix: Cover loosely for the first 24 hours. At leather-hard, place a second flat board on top under light weight to press the base flat while it dries

items.problem: Rim wall falls away from the base during joining
items.cause: The scored surfaces were not wet enough with slip, or the clay stiffened too much before the join was made
items.fix: Re-score both faces, apply generous slip, and press again. Support the wall from the outside with a coil of clay or a folded cloth while it firms

items.problem: Corner joins crack at the meeting point of the two rim strips
items.cause: The two strips shrank at slightly different rates, opening the corner join
items.fix: At leather-hard, fill the crack with fresh slip, press a thin clay coil into the crack, and smooth. Allow to dry slowly

items.problem: Rim walls are not vertical when viewed from above
items.cause: The strips were pressed in slightly inward or outward during joining
items.fix: Correct the angle at the joining stage before the clay stiffens. After the board has dried, slight lean cannot be reversed without risk of cracking
